provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

negative

value.reason: server.ts:294 serves the 'ftp' directory publicly at '/ftp' using serveIndex with directory listing turned on. The only middleware in front of it is serveIndexMiddleware, and it is not an authorization check like the security.isAuthorized() call in the negative example. The line also carries the repo's own 'vuln-line directoryListingChallenge' marker. The data flow shows routes/order.ts:45 writing generated order PDFs into 'ftp/' with fs.createWriteStream(path.join('ftp/', pdfFile)). So per-customer order documents, which hold customer and order details, land in a directory that anyone can browse and download without logging in. This matches the positive example: an unauthenticated serveIndex directory plus a write of personal data into it. Without access control, this falls short of the requirement for reasonable security safeguards and access control over computer resources. The UserId model snippets do not affect the verdict. One caveat: the evidence does not show the PDF contents or the body of serveIndexMiddleware, but the public listing, the write into that directory and the vulnerability marker are enough to support the finding.
